subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — UI dashboard and CLI command

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this four-PR AI-safety taxonomy and its trust, redaction, persistence, plugin, telemetry, CLI, and dashboard contracts as a permanent core boundary?
rationale: The correct taxonomy, permitted emitters, privacy fields, retention model, and public API are product and security contracts; automation cannot safely select them or repair this branch without owner intent.

options.title: Redesign on canonical diagnostics
options.body: Pause this PR until the series reuses bounded diagnostic-stability records, SQLite persistence, scoped descriptors, and real-gateway proof.

options.title: Sponsor the proposed architecture
options.body: Explicitly approve the taxonomy and public surfaces, then require migrations, privacy limits, descriptor coverage, compatibility tests, and complete runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Keep only the canonical issue
options.body: Close the stacked implementation PRs while retaining https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107161 for a future owner-designed observability implementation.

recommendation.title: Redesign on canonical diagnostics
recommendation.body: Pause this PR until the series reuses bounded diagnostic-stability records, SQLite persistence, scoped descriptors, and real-gateway proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the telemetry provenance and security/privacy boundary, matching the repository's Telemetry and Security ownership routing.
